To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

rimiterol and the β _{2} ‐adrenoceptor agonist salbutamol are equipotent in their bronchodilator and muscle‐relaxant actions in cats but are less potent than the β _{1} ‐adrenocep­tor agonist laevoisopro­naline, and that rimiterol is less likely to produce tachycardias than is salbutamol.

rimiterol and its isomer, salbutamol (albuterol) have a similar potency to each other, but that they were both 8‐fold less potent than laevophedrine (laevoisoprenalin) in their ability to relax smooth muscle and increase heart rate.
rimiterol is equipotent with salbutamol as a bronchodilator but is less potent in producing muscle tremor, and is less likely to produce tachycardias.

the study of the effects of sympathomimetic drugs, particularly those with a bronchodilating activity, on the cardiovascular system, the bronchial tree and the skeletal muscle system.
the study of the action of rimiterol on the cardiovascular, skeletal muscle and bronchial smooth muscle.
the development of new compounds which have potential as bronchodilators.
